patch.value: Make the release gate deterministic: a clock-dependent changelog date and a branch V8 reported inconsistently

Two gates in this package passed or failed on something other than the code under test. The changelog heading for an unreleased version was stamped from the local calendar date, so a host at UTC+2 generating after 22:00 UTC produced tomorrow's date and CI regenerated today's, failing check on an otherwise identical commit. That defect was fixed upstream in pm-changelog 2026.8.2, but this package still pinned 2026.7.29-1 in its lockfile, so the fix had never actually arrived and the workaround of regenerating under TZ=UTC was being reapplied by hand. Separately the coverage gate failed at 99.49 percent branches on model.ts in one CI job while the other job on the same commit reported 100, and the same split appeared locally across runs. The cause was not flakiness in the gate: decodeTree had a genuinely uncovered arm, the non-array case of an entry line that parses as JSON, and V8 attributed that block as covered in some runs and not others. The gate was reporting a real gap intermittently rather than inventing one.

pm-changelog is upgraded to a version that derives release dates in UTC, and generating under TZ=UTC and TZ=Europe/Vienna at the same instant produces byte-identical output; the changelog no longer needs a TZ override to pass check; decodeTree refuses a tree entry line that parses to a non-array, covered by an explicit test for both an object and a scalar; three consecutive coverage runs report 100 percent lines, branches and functions with no variation; release:check exits zero end to end

pm-changelog upgraded to 2026.8.2 and byte-identical output verified across TZ=UTC and TZ=Europe/Vienna at one instant; decodeTree's non-array arm covered for both an object and a scalar entry; three consecutive coverage runs reported 100/100/100 with no variation; release:check exits zero.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Reopened scope on verification: the UTC upgrade this item delivered fixed timezone drift but not clock dependence. With no release tag in a gated repo, pm-changelog falls back to the current date, so the committed heading was 2026.7.30 - 2026-08-03 - the version's number and the day it happened to be generated. changelog:check therefore passed only on its generation day and would have failed on main the next morning. Every released package in the fleet pairs the version with its own CalVer date (2026.7.29 - 2026-07-29), so the heading was also inconsistent with the convention. Fixed by pinning --date 2026-07-30 across changelog, changelog:full and changelog:check and correcting the committed heading. The gate is now independent of when it runs, which is what this item claimed.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Release-time caveat for whoever lifts the gate on this package. The --date 2026-07-30 pin now in changelog, changelog:full and changelog:check is an unconditional override, not a fallback: pm-changelog has no fallback-shaped flag today. It is correct while this package is release-gated and therefore untagged, because without a tag the only alternative is the current date and the committed heading then expires nightly. The moment a real release tag exists that pin will win over the tag's own date and the heading will be wrong in a new way. Removing the three pins is therefore part of lifting the release gate, not an optional cleanup. Filed upstream on pm-changelog as issue 120, asking for a --date-fallback that defers to a tag when one exists, or a --date-from-version that derives the fallback from the CalVer version so no pin is needed at all.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review found the pin was not applied end to end. release:notes, which the release workflow uses to build the GitHub release body, invoked pm-changelog without --date while changelog:check and the prepublish gate used the pinned one. The gate and the artefact it gates could therefore have disagreed about the release date. All four pm-changelog invocations in this package now carry --date 2026-07-30, so there is one release-date source rather than two. This does not change the release-time caveat: all four pins come out together when the gate is lifted, not three of them.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Third and final set of invocation sites. The release workflow does not call the npm scripts; it spells the pm-changelog command out again in three run steps, so pinning the four package.json scripts left those three unpinned and the claim of one release-date source was still false. All seven sites in this package now carry --date 2026-07-30. The underlying cause is the duplication itself: the same command exists in seven places with slightly different flags, so any per-site fix has to be repeated seven times and silently rots when one is missed. The durable fix is for the workflow to invoke the npm scripts rather than restate them, which would leave exactly one place to pin and one place to unpin when the release gate is lifted. Not done here because changing the release path of a gated package is a larger change than the defect being fixed, and the workflow steps differ from the scripts in --pm-bin and in redirecting to RELEASE_NOTES.md rather than the step summary.

patch.value: Every pm-changelog invocation in the package resolves the same release date, across all four package.json scripts and all three npx calls in the release workflow, so the gate and the artefact it gates cannot disagree; changelog:check passes under each of TZ=UTC, TZ=Etc/GMT+12 and TZ=Etc/GMT-14, the three being required together because the minus-twelve zone is on the previous UTC date only while the UTC time of day is before 12:00 and the plus-fourteen zone is on the next one only from 10:00, so their union leaves no hour at which the check fails to cross a calendar-date boundary; the committed heading pairs the version with the CalVer date that version encodes; the record states that the pin is an override rather than a fallback and must be removed when the release gate is lifted

patch.value: The gate no longer depends on when or where it runs, and the release path no longer depends on a static pin. Verified at 2026-08-03T08:45:59Z: changelog:check passes under each of TZ=UTC, TZ=Etc/GMT+12 and TZ=Etc/GMT-14 - TZ=UTC:PASS TZ=Etc/GMT+12:PASS TZ=Etc/GMT-14:PASS. The three zones are required together because the minus-twelve zone is on the previous UTC date only before 12:00 UTC and the plus-fourteen zone is on the next one only from 10:00, so their union leaves no hour where the check stops crossing a date boundary.

Two distinct fixes. Locally, the four package.json changelog scripts pin --date 2026-07-30 so the gate is independent of the day it runs while this package is untagged. In the release workflow, the three npx pm-changelog calls take their date from a new release_iso_date output derived from the year, month and day the tag itself encodes, so a release cannot publish a version whose changelog heading names a different day than the version. Seven invocation sites in total, none of them now reading the clock.

changelog:check passes under all three zones at 2026-08-03T08:45:59Z - TZ=UTC:PASS TZ=Etc/GMT+12:PASS TZ=Etc/GMT-14:PASS. The workflow derives its date from the tag, so the static pin no longer reaches the release path.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review found the static pin would have reached the release path: the Decide release step builds the tag from a computed version while the changelog commands passed a fixed date, so a release could have published a version whose heading named a different day. The workflow now derives release_iso_date from the year, month and day the tag already encodes and passes that instead. The local scripts keep the static pin, which is correct because they run against an untagged tree where no tag date exists to derive from. That also narrows the release-gate caveat: the four script pins still come out when the gate is lifted, but the workflow is now correct by construction rather than by remembering.
